boundary: The ordinary frozen Node HTTP server connection listener and native Gateway::serve_connection operate on bounded synthetic in-memory HTTP/1 sockets. A fixed raw request body, headers and idle keep-alive downstream connection are prepared outside each sample. Start immediately before making the request bytes readable. End after the ordinary handler, actual response observation, final downstream HTTP framing/write/flush and continuation confirmation finish, and every advisory count reply completes. Internal event-loop/runtime scheduling remains included; there is no percentile subtraction or separately timed pure policy call.
workload: Exact local-benchmark-v3 large_catalog_miss fixture,300 tools,30 description repetitions,compatible profile,source claude-opus-5-5,confidence1 sonnet evaluator answer and one Haiku advisory count reporting1000 input tokens. One sequential client with unique12-digit content index and prompt identity for each miss. upstream: Inference uses genuine Node http.request and the native pinned Hyper-util HTTP client, including HTTP/1 request serialization, response parsing and body streaming, through bounded immediate synthetic sockets/connectors. Every synthetic connector refuses all destinations except the declared127.0.0.1:1 origin and fixed inference path. The same client builder/request policy logic is shared with production, with retries disabled. No TCP,DNS,TLS,provider or model operation exists in this path. Evaluator/count use supported immediate injectable boundaries and the real classifier/token-counter parsing/cache/finally machinery; their external client connection establishment is excluded. If a first slice lacks either genuine inference codec or ordinary-loopback equivalence, its report must explicitly mark the whole-gateway0.5 gate incomplete.

downstream HTTP serialization and clean final write/flush

verification: Retain fixture/protocol/source/adapter/compiler/Node/native-helper hashes. Require exact prepared body and response application bytes, meaningful canonical headers/status, complete ordered evaluator/count/inference payload hashes, one evaluator/one count/one inference per miss, complete count reply parsing with zero abandonment, actual successful continuation confirmation and clean close. Compare every non-clock decision and lifecycle field after only explicit random request-id/timestamp/duration normalization. A separate ordinary-loopback control runs the same ordinary handler and actual client without synthetic socket injection and must match all request/response/call/state hashes before any numerical comparison. Invalid credentials, oversized wire, forbidden connector destinations and incomplete writer/count completion must fail validation. Synthetic validation is not real evaluator or hardware evidence.
